Quality engineering.d: A modern view of QA in which testers help build quality in from the start (requirements, design, automation, monitoring) rather than only checking finished software at the end.

Shift-left testing.d: Moving testing activities earlier in the development process, for example reviewing requirements for gaps before any code is written, so problems are found when they are cheapest to fix.

Exploratory testing.d: Testing where the tester designs and runs tests at the same time, learning about the product as they go, instead of following a fixed script.

Flaky test.d: An automated test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any change to the code, usually because of timing, shared data or unstable environments.

Regression testing.d: Re-testing existing features after a change to make sure nothing that used to work has broken.

Test oracle.d: Whatever tells you the correct expected result for a test: a requirement, a rule, a previous version, or a person's judgement.

Context engineering.d: Deciding everything an AI model gets to see for a task (instructions, examples, documents, tool results, memory files) and what to leave out, so it can do the job well.

Impact-effort matrix.d: A simple 2×2 grid for prioritising ideas: how much value each would bring against how much work it takes. Start with high-impact, low-effort ideas.
